evidence.title: Complementary activity of tyrosine kinase inhibitors against secondary kit mutations in imatinib-resistant gastrointestinal stromal tumours.
evidence.finding: Patient-derived GIST models show complementary inhibitor activity across secondary KIT mutations. V654A, T670I and activation-loop variants do not share one sensitivity profile. This supports genotype-resolved screening rather than WT-only ranking.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence.title: Avapritinib Versus Regorafenib in Locally Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic GI Stromal Tumor: A Randomized, Open-Label Phase III Study.
evidence.finding: VOYAGER did not demonstrate superior PFS for avapritinib over regorafenib in molecularly unselected third-line or later GIST. This finding is population-specific and does not negate activity in PDGFRA D842V disease.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence.title: Ripretinib Versus Sunitinib in Patients With Advanced Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor After Treatment With Imatinib (INTRIGUE): A Randomized, Open-Label, Phase III Trial.
evidence.finding: INTRIGUE did not demonstrate superior PFS for second-line ripretinib over sunitinib. Activity and tolerability findings remain relevant; a missed superiority endpoint is not proof of no activity.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence.title: Ripretinib versus sunitinib in gastrointestinal stromal tumor: ctDNA biomarker analysis of the phase 3 INTRIGUE trial.
evidence.finding: Exploratory INTRIGUE ctDNA analyses suggest different relative treatment effects in KIT exon 11 plus 13/14 versus exon 11 plus 17/18 populations. These subgroup results are hypothesis-generating, not a replacement for a prospective genotype-specific trial.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; source findings curated against primary publication

evidence.title: Heterogeneity of kinase inhibitor resistance mechanisms in GIST.
evidence.finding: Different metastases and subclones can harbor different secondary resistance mutations; KIT loss and amplification were also observed. A single mutation model cannot represent every escape mechanism.
evidence.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication

evidence.title: Phase I dose escalation study of NMS-1286937, an orally available Polo-Like Kinase 1 inhibitor, in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors.
evidence.finding: A phase I study of the PLK1 inhibitor NMS-1286937 reported thrombocytopenia and neutropenia as major dose-limiting toxicities. This motivates PLK1 as an anti-target to assess; it does not establish PLK1 as the cause of toxicity for KIT inhibitors.
evidence.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication
evidence.scope: External anti-target background; not a GIST program or evidence of KIT-inhibitor toxicity causality

evidence.title: Experimental and computational approaches to estimate solubility and permeability in drug discovery and development settings.
evidence.finding: Physicochemical heuristics identify oral absorption and permeation risk. Treat molecular weight, lipophilicity and hydrogen-bond counts as triage flags rather than universal exclusion rules for kinase inhibitors.
evidence.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication

evidence.title: Association of Combination of Conformation-Specific KIT Inhibitors With Clinical Benefit in Patients With Refractory Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors: A Phase 1b/2a Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.finding: A small nonrandomized phase 1b/2a study investigated conformation-complementary KIT inhibitors PLX9486 and sunitinib in refractory GIST. Combination activity is an experimental clinical observation, not evidence that arbitrary co-dependent targets make effective combinations.
evidence.retrieval: Europe PMC metadata; analyst-reviewed primary publication

evidence.title: ADMET-AI: a machine learning ADMET platform for evaluation of large-scale chemical libraries
evidence.finding: ADMET-AI provides learned ADMET endpoints and computed physicochemical descriptors. Half-life and distribution predictions require particular caution; endpoint predictions do not establish a dose-to-tumor-response PK/PD model.
evidence.retrieval: Primary methods paper and current model endpoint metadata

evidence.title: Ptarmigan-1 API reference
evidence.finding: Only catalog human proteins may be screened through the current API. Engagement probability is a prediction, not IC50; fixed probability cutoffs do not establish binding. Reference proteome off-target predictions are web-app only.
evidence.retrieval: Official OpenAPI and agent documentation

evidence.title: DepMap co-dependency scoring
evidence.finding: DepMap co-dependency is based on Pearson correlation of dependency profiles. Correlation alone does not establish synthetic lethality, resistance causality or clinical combination efficacy.
evidence.retrieval: Official DepMap community explanation

evidence.title: Proteome Phenome Atlas
evidence.finding: Plasma protein associations are distinct from tumor somatic genotype and target-inhibition effects. KIT assay membership must be checked in an identified complete panel table before reporting presence or absence.
evidence.retrieval: Official atlas

evidence.title: Effects of CYP3A Inhibition, CYP3A Induction, and Gastric Acid Reduction on the Pharmacokinetics of Ripretinib, a Switch Control KIT Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor.
evidence.finding: A healthy-participant drug-interaction study measured changes in ripretinib exposure, elimination half-life and apparent clearance with CYP3A inhibition or induction. These are observed, regimen-specific PK results; they cannot be transferred as numerical requirements for another compound.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip CLI gateway; full source passage checked locally

evidence.title: Switch Control Inhibition of KIT and PDGFRA in Patients With Advanced Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor: A Phase I Study of Ripretinib.
evidence.finding: The phase I ripretinib study reports dose- and time-specific plasma exposure, an active metabolite and a preclinical exposure rationale. Total plasma concentrations do not directly establish unbound tumor exposure or occupancy.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip CLI gateway; full source passage checked locally

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — ADME/T Properties
evidence.finding: MW and calculated lipophilicity jointly influence developability. The suggested favorable MW/logP region is a heuristic; compounds outside it can still be developable. Early model flags should lead to staged measurements.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Solubility
evidence.finding: Solubility interpretation depends on dose, pH, formulation and assay method. Poor assay solubility can distort activity and ADME results; kinetic and equilibrium solubility are distinct.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — hERG Blockers
evidence.finding: Assess functional hERG activity against exposure, with attention to free drug and additional cardiac ion channels. A roughly 30-fold hERG IC50/Cmax margin is discussed as a heuristic, not a guarantee of cardiac safety; global predictors can lose external performance.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Predicting Off-target Activity
evidence.finding: Target profiling requires a distinct model or counter-screen. Predictions depend on annotated activity data and applicability; they can guide follow-up for potential cross-reactivity.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Separation of PK and PD
evidence.finding: Duration of action may reflect binding residence time or active metabolites. Equilibrium affinity alone cannot determine off-rate; plasma half-life should not be substituted for pharmacodynamic duration.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Kinase Inhibitors
evidence.finding: Kinase binding depends on conserved catalytic-site features and conformation. Type I and type II binding modes highlight why mutant sequence and conformational context matter.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Cambridge MedChem Consulting — Lipophilicity
evidence.finding: Calculated logP methods differ, and logP is distinct from pH-dependent logD. Lipophilicity influences solubility, distribution and off-target liabilities, supporting multi-property assessment rather than a single threshold.
evidence.retrieval: User-specified guidance reviewed 2026-11-14; historical publication date not asserted

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of imatinib mesylate in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors.
evidence.finding: In 147 patients with advanced GIST receiving 400 or 600 mg imatinib daily, 53.7% had a partial response and 27.9% stable disease. Imatinib is the successful efficacy benchmark; acquired resistance is a distinct limitation.
evidence.retrieval: Primary trial publication, PubMed abstract checked

evidence.title: Ripretinib in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours (INVICTUS): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
evidence.finding: After at least imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib, median progression-free survival was 6.3 months with ripretinib versus 1.0 with placebo. Its later second-line INTRIGUE superiority endpoint is a separate question.
evidence.retrieval: Primary trial publication, results checked

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of sunitinib in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour after failure of imatinib: a randomised controlled trial.
evidence.finding: In 312 randomized patients with imatinib-resistant or intolerant GIST, median time to tumour progression was 27.3 weeks on sunitinib versus 6.4 weeks on placebo.
evidence.retrieval: Primary trial publication, PubMed abstract checked

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of regorafenib for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours after failure of imatinib and sunitinib (GRID).
evidence.finding: In 199 randomized patients after imatinib and sunitinib, median progression-free survival was 4.8 months with regorafenib versus 0.9 with placebo.
evidence.retrieval: Primary trial publication, results checked

evidence.title: Evaluation of nilotinib in advanced GIST previously treated with imatinib and sunitinib
evidence.finding: Nilotinib was tolerated in imatinib- and sunitinib-refractory advanced GIST but did not deliver sufficient clinical benefit to support further development in the unselected refractory population; activity was suggested in an exon 17 subset.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; curated against primary publication

evidence.title: Emerging mechanisms of kinase inhibitor escape and clinical implications of ponatinib in advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor
evidence.finding: Ponatinib covers the T670I gatekeeper and multiple activation-loop mutants but is resisted by the ATP-pocket V654A mutation. Early 45 mg dosing was limited by significant cardiovascular toxicity; at 30 mg clinical benefit remained limited (approximately 26% at 16 weeks second-line, 33% late-line). Cardiovascular toxicity is the defining concern.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; curated against primary publication

evidence.title: Vatalanib for metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) resistant to imatinib: final results of a phase II study
evidence.finding: Vatalanib showed activity in imatinib-resistant metastatic GIST in a single-arm phase II study, with clinical benefit in approximately 40% of patients. Development did not progress to a randomised registration trial in GIST.
evidence.retrieval: Paperclip document metadata; curated against primary publication

criteria.policy_rationale: 0.5 is a provisional model triage flag, not an exposure safety margin or a clinical QT threshold.

criteria.criterion: Activity against the chosen driver-plus-resistance profile
criteria.measurable_by: Genotype-matched functional assays or a calibrated mutant-capable model
criteria.policy_rationale: Require coverage of the declared mutation panel before calling a candidate genotype-qualified. Coverage definition and assay potency thresholds must be prespecified.

Hypertension and hand-foot skin reaction are documented for the VEGFR-active multikinase inhibitors used in GIST (sunitinib, regorafenib). Mechanistic attribution to VEGFR2 is inference, not established causation, so this is a weighted flag rather than a hard gate. The 30-fold margin is configurable policy, not a published safe threshold.
Sequence-level screening cannot establish control of heterogeneous or KIT-independent disease.
Trial interpretation requires genotype, line of therapy and comparator; aggregate failure is not universal inactivity.
ADMET endpoint predictions do not establish human unbound tumor exposure, target occupancy or dose-response. Published PK/PD and functional potency must be reconciled.
Flag MW >400 Da together with computed logP >4 as a less favorable developability region. This is a weighted risk flag; calculated methods differ and exceptions remain possible.
Provisional 0.5 model probability flag. A substrate/inhibitor probability is an input to DDI assessment; it does not predict a clinical interaction magnitude.
Provisional model probability flag for follow-up, not an observed clinical liver-injury rate.

criteria.measurable_by: Functional hERG IC50 and justified unbound Cmax
criteria.policy_rationale: 30-fold is a configurable triage margin discussed in the guidance, not guaranteed freedom from cardiac toxicity. hERG classifier probability cannot populate this metric.
Review experimental kinetic/equilibrium solubility, pH and intended concentration. A structure-only logS prediction cannot settle assay interference or dose feasibility.
Affinity and plasma half-life do not determine target residence time or PD duration. Retain this as a review question until kinetics and metabolite data exist.
Ripretinib DDI evidence motivates checking CYP3A-mediated clearance. A high substrate prediction is a weighted follow-up flag, not an exclusion or a forecast of clinical DDI magnitude.

Use engagement as a continuous prioritization signal. The zero threshold denotes the valid score range, not an engagement cutoff. This signal never satisfies mutant-activity requirements. Weight 20 explicitly prioritizes the user-requested target-engagement signal over individual property flags; it is configurable policy, not an experimentally fitted weight.

criteria.measurable_by: Genotype-matched KIT Kd assay or independently calibrated affinity estimate
criteria.policy_rationale: Provisional discovery gate of Kd ≤1 µM, pending target-specific calibration. Engagement probability, raw cosine, cellular IC50 and docking confidence cannot be substituted for Kd. Missing potency remains unqualified; the threshold does not establish efficacy.

VOYAGER missed PFS superiority in unselected later-line GIST; PDGFRA D842V benefit is a separate population.

programs.why_stopped: Insufficient clinical benefit in imatinib- and sunitinib-refractory GIST; not advanced in the unselected refractory population.
programs.role: Developed as a second-generation KIT/ABL inhibitor for refractory GIST; did not establish benefit in the unselected refractory setting.

programs.why_stopped: Cardiovascular toxicity at 45 mg and limited overall activity; V654A ATP-pocket resistance restricts the eligible genotype.
programs.role: Type II inhibitor engineered for the T670I gatekeeper; covers activation-loop mutants but not V654A, and carries arterial occlusive risk.

programs.why_stopped: Activity shown only in a single-arm phase II; no randomised registration trial followed in GIST.
